**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 98 **Price** 13,000 gp --- This huge, magical clockwork rover moves on a continuous band of heavy treads, which make it easier to for the device to navigate across various adverse conditions. It contains magical clockwork birds which can transmit visual information back to the surveyor. --- **Space** 15 feet long, 15 feet wide, 20 feet high **Crew** pilot, 2 crew **Passengers** 7 **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 32) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 34) --- **AC** 33 **Fort** +25 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 190 (BT 95) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 15 feet ([clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=874), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 8d12 (DC 30) **Continuous Track** This vehicle travels on a continuous band of heavy treads driven by a series of gears and wheels, enabling it to travel over rugged land with ease. Earth, rock, rubble, slopes, and underbrush are not difficult terrain to an ambling surveyor. The ambling surveyor [ignores difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) from earth, rock, rubble, slopes, and underbrush, and greater difficult terrain caused by those features is normal difficult terrain to the ambling surveyor.
**Sluggish** This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.
**Survey** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [exploration](/Skills.aspx?ID=23), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Requirements** The ambling surveyor is not in motion; **Effect** The pilot and crew release a collection of six clockwork birds, which spend two hours flying over the surrounding area within a 1-mile radius around the ambling surveyor. Everything the birds see is magically transmitted back to the ambling surveyor’s crew as illusory images, which the crew must catalogue in real-time if they want to use the information to fully survey the area and create a map. After two hours, the birds return. The birds use the base statistics of [clockwork spies](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1095) if they are attacked, or if their Perception is important to determine what they can see, although they only perform the Survey action and they don’t have any of the other abilities of a clockwork spy. Replacement birds cost 250 gp each.
**Wind-Up** 10 minutes of wind‑up, 1 hour of operational time, DC 32, standby

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 97 **Price** 4,000 gp --- This apparatus, which is shaped like an octopus (or more rarely, a squid or other aquatic creature), uses almost entirely magical propulsion. Clockwork parts make up the controls and mechanisms to improve some of the functionality, but magic moves the vehicles’ cogs and gears. While it needs only a pilot, it can optionally hold a second crew member, which can be useful if the second crew member controls the apparatus’s hands or eyes. --- **Space** 10 feet long, 10 feet wide, 5 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot **Passengers** 1 ((the passenger can optionally act as crew but more crew isn’t necessary)) **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 28) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 30) --- **AC** 25 **Fort** +20 **Hardness** 15 **HP** 150 (BT 75) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 5 feet, swim 40 feet ([clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=874), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 7d10 (DC 28) Manipulate Hands (Interact) A crew member operates a lever set up like a joystick, allowing that crew member to extend and manipulate the apparatus’s hands. While the hands can’t attack and can’t perform fine actions such as [Disabling a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411), [Stealing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2410) something, or opening the stopper on a potion bottle, but they can grasp and hold up to 50 Bulk.
**Open Eyes** (Interact) A crew member pulls a lever to open the apparatus’s eyes, which shine [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) within 20 feet and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet. A crew member can take this action again to close the eyes. Open
**Portholes** (Interact) A crew member pulls a lever to open two portholes, allowing the crew to see outside the apparatus and other creatures to see into it. A crew member can take this action again to close the portholes.
**Submersible** The apparatus of the octopus can protect its crew and passengers from water pressure to a maximum depth of 5,000 feet and contains enough air for 12 hours for a pilot alone or 6 hours for a pilot and passenger or crew member.

fields.text: Vehicle 11 Apparatus of The Octopus Uncommon Medium Source Guns & Gears pg. 97 Price 4,000 gp This apparatus, which is shaped like an octopus (or more rarely, a squid or other aquatic creature), uses almost entirely magical propulsion. Clockwork parts make up the controls and mechanisms to improve some of the functionality, but magic moves the vehicles’ cogs and gears. While it needs only a pilot, it can optionally hold a second crew member, which can be useful if the second crew member controls the apparatus’s hands or eyes. Space 10 feet long, 10 feet wide, 5 feet high Crew 1 pilot Passengers 1 ((the passenger can optionally act as crew but more crew isn’t necessary)) Piloting Check Driving Lore (DC 28) or Crafting (DC 30) AC 25 Fort +20 Hardness 15 HP 150 (BT 75) Immunities object immunities Speed 5 feet, swim 40 feet (clockwork, magical) Collision 7d10 (DC 28) Manipulate Hands Two Actions (Interact) A crew member operates a lever set up like a joystick, allowing that crew member to extend and manipulate the apparatus’s hands. While the hands can’t attack and can’t perform fine actions such as Disabling a Device, Stealing something, or opening the stopper on a potion bottle, but they can grasp and hold up to 50 Bulk. Open Eyes Two Actions (Interact) A crew member pulls a lever to open the apparatus’s eyes, which shine bright light within 20 feet and dim light for the next 20 feet. A crew member can take this action again to close the eyes. Open Portholes Two Actions (Interact) A crew member pulls a lever to open two portholes, allowing the crew to see outside the apparatus and other creatures to see into it. A crew member can take this action again to close the portholes. Submersible The apparatus of the octopus can protect its crew and passengers from water pressure to a maximum depth of 5,000 feet and contains enough air for 12 hours for a pilot alone or 6 hours for a pilot and passenger or crew member.

<traits>
<trait label="Huge" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 266

**Price** 4,000 gp

</column>

---

The structure of these gargantuan vessels is fully covered by iron. These vessels are akin to floating fortresses rather than true warships, and are typically used in coastal actions and for river blockades. They use oars for propulsion, as their full iron cladding, as well as their bulk, impedes propulsion via sails.

 Many of these vessels are beautifully gilded with red and gold inlays across their iron cladding. This added weight only further contributes to their suspect stability.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 75 feet long, 30 feet wide, 30 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 80 rowers

**Passengers** 60
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 27), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 29), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 29)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 26

**Fort** +21

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 20

**HP** 150 (BT 75)

**Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** swim 30 feet (rowed)

**Collision** 8d10 (DC 27)

**Sluggish** This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.

</column>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Gargantuan" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 94

**Price** 240,000 gp

</column>

---

The majestic _Augustana's Pride_ is usually kept docked at its eponymous port, but is put on active duty in times of great need. Constructed almost entirely of duskwood, with accents painted in Andoren blue and gold, this warship is the crowning jewel of the navy.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 280 feet long, 40 feet wide, 30 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 50 crew

**Passengers** 50
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Sailing Lore (DC 40)](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 42), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 42)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 40

**Fort** +34

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 20

**HP** 300 (BT 150)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

**Weaknesses** fire 20 until broken
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** swim 35 feet (wind)

**Collision** 14d10 (DC 40)

**Inspiring Presence** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) 300 feet. The sight of the Andoren navy's flagship bolsters its fleet and its crew. At the beginning of their turns or when they enter the aura, allied creatures on board the ship and allied creatures within a 300-foot-emanation who can see the ship gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, and saves against fear for 1 round.

 **Weapon Mounts** This vehicle has 6 weapon mounts, three on each side of the vehicle. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a mount requires 1 day, a successful DC 40 Crafting check, and an appropriate weapon. The weapon mounts can be equipped with Huge or smaller ranged [siege weapons](/SiegeWeapons.aspx).

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 266

**Price** 8,000 gp

---

The keel of these vessels consists of wooden beams bound together with iron hoops to provide added stability during ocean transits. In stormy weather, holes in the prow partially fill with water when the ship pitches forward, lessening the violent turbulence caused by waves. Renowned for their seaworthiness, Baochuan were often chosen for transporting valuable treasure or important emissaries during stormy seasons. As such, they're often referred to as “treasure ships” and highly sought prizes by pirates.

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 177 **Price** 30,000 gp --- The battery tower uses both pushed propulsion and turned propulsion to turn a capstan. Turned propulsion uses the same rules as rowed propulsion. Pushed propulsion uses the same rules as pulled. --- **Space** 50 feet long, 50 feet wide, 90 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 150 turners, 2,200 pushers **Passengers** 204 **Piloting Check** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 37), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 37), or [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 35) --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +28 **Hardness** 25 **HP** 150 (BT 75) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 10 feet (pushed, turned) **Collision** 8d10 (DC 32) **Sluggish** This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.
**Tiered** A battery tower has five levels. The crew operate at the bottom tier, turning a giant capstan, and up to four passengers can fit on that floor, enough for a full crew for a bombard. The remaining levels carry 50 passengers each. The tiers are specifically meant to be protective, and give those within the battery tower greater cover (or standard cover if the battery tower is broken). A massive ladder runs diagonally through the center of the battery tower, from the front of the top tier to the rear of the bottom tier. The ladder is wide enough for two crew or passengers to climb simultaneously.
**Weaponry** A battery tower is usually loaded with black powder siege weapons for heavy assaults, with bombards on the bottom two floors and cannons on the other floors. Their Price is included in that of the battery tower. When building a battery tower, you can choose to replace any of these with other siege weapons of a lower Price. If you want a more expensive siege weapon, you must Craft it separately. Passengers of the battery tower can crew these siege weapons.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 76 --- This hand-woven coracle appears large enough to hold only a single person. When you pilot the boat, however, you can take on up to a dozen passengers, which ride in your soul. While there, their bodies and equipment are absorbed into you—they are aware of everything you sense and can communicate telepathically with you or any other passengers, but otherwise can't act except to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) and use actions that require only the use of their mind (as determined by the GM). They can exit your soul, or you can remove any number of them using a single action—which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait—causing them to appear in a space adjacent to _Bunta_. If you leave _Bunta_ or are killed, any creatures in your soul immediately exit your body into the nearest available space. If you leave _Bunta_ after piloting it, you can use a single action, which has the concentrate trait, to store the boat in your soul. You can remove it from your soul into an adjacent square with another such action. **Spirit Ship** _Bunta_ can be damaged by spells like [_spirit blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=301) that damage a creature's spirit directly, and such effects ignore _Bunta's_ hardness. --- **Speed** fly 40 feet (magical), swim 40 feet (magical), swim 20 feet (rowed) **Collision** secret of souls **Activate** command, envision, Interact; **Requirements** You are piloting _Bunta_; **Effect** A silver river flows from your heart, traveling forward in a line that flows around obstacles as if it were water. If you continue, you have a 1% cumulative chance of ending up in a random extraplanar location for each round that _Bunta_ did not travel at least its Speed, to a maximum of a 60% chance if _Bunta_ didn't travel at least its Speed for the full 10 minutes. As long as you remain on _Bunta_, you are protected from any harmful effects of the plane's environment.

<title level="1" right="Vehicle 6">[Cauldron of Flying](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=53)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Medium" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #182: Graveclaw](/Sources.aspx?ID=143) pg. 79

**Price** 1,100 gp

</column>

---

Witches flying about the countryside at night in their magical cauldrons are often merely legends, but the existence of this magical vehicle shows at least some of the legends are true.

 A _cauldron of flying_ can carry only one creature, who stands or crouches in the cauldron and steers it with a ladle, broomstick, or similar implement. The specific implement isn't part of the cauldron and doesn't need to have any particular magic; it simply focuses the pilot's desire to have the cauldron soar into the air and direct it where the pilot wants it to go.

 When not in use as a vehicle, the cauldron can be used to boil food and prepare alchemical ingredients, just like any mundane cauldron. To activate the cauldron, however, it must be empty.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** A large cooking pot 4 feet high and 5 feet in diameter, bulging slightly in the middle and flaring at the top.

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot

</row>

**Piloting Check** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) (DC 24), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (DC 20), or [Piloting Lore](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1969) (DC 22)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 21

**Fort** +14

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 9

**HP** 79 (BT 36)

**Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** fly 30 feet (magical)

**Collision** 4d8 (DC 22)

**Iron Rim** <actions string="Single Action" /> The cauldron provides its pilot with standard cover, although this cover doesn't typically provide any bonus to Stealth checks, as a flying cauldron is both visible and suspicious.

</column>

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 111 **Price** 210,000 gp --- This massive undead vehicle is created by crafting a piloting and cargo compartment within the husk of a massive cave worm and then infusing the remains with void energy. This compartment has breathable air as well as sealable weapon ports. Designed specifically to burrow under and then behind enemy positions, cavern crawlers can attack enemies on their flank or bring supplies and reinforcements to troops deep behind enemy lines. --- **Space** 100 feet long, 30 feet wide, 30 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 3 crew **Passengers** 30 **Piloting Check** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (DC 42) or [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 40) --- **AC** 43 **Fort** +34 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 300 (BT 150) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage --- **Speed** 30 feet, burrow 30 feet ([clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=331), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 14d10 (DC 40) **Swallow** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) Two crew members each perform a 3-action activity on their turn to open the caravan crawler’s mouth and eat a Huge or smaller creature adjacent to the vehicle, who must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude save. A creature can choose to fail. On a failure, the creature is swallowed by the cavern crawler, moved into the passenger bay, and knocked prone. This action fails if the passenger bay is full.
**Tunnel** The cavern crawler can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 15 feet. The pilot can choose to leave a tunnel.

A creature can choose to fail. On a failure, the creature is swallowed by the cavern crawler, moved into the passenger bay, and knocked prone. This action fails if the passenger bay is full. Tunnel The cavern crawler can burrow through solid stone at a Speed of 15 feet. The pilot can choose to leave a tunnel.

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 96 **Price** 2,100 gp --- A clockwork borer is essentially a huge adamantine drill attached to a large wheeled carriage. The clockwork gears within move the borer itself and spin the drill, allowing it to burrow through loose material quickly and even through solid stone at a slower rate. --- **Space** 20 feet long, 8 feet wide, 8 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot **Passengers** 5 **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 26) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 28) --- **AC** 24 **Fort** +18 **Hardness** 15 **HP** 110 (BT 55) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 20 feet, burrow 10 feet (clockwork) **Collision** 6d10 piercing (DC 26) **Adamantine Drill** While most burrow Speeds only allow a creature or vehicle to move through loose dirt or earth, this vehicle is equipped with an [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915) drill and can burrow through bedrock and stone at a rate of 5 feet per minute.
**Pivoting Seats** This vehicle’s seats are mounted on a weighted platform that pivots as the vehicle moves, automatically adjusting position with gravity. Seated creatures remain upright no matter the position or angle of the vehicle.
**Sluggish** Because it is sluggish, this vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.
**Wind-Up** 10 minutes of wind-up, 1 hour of operational time, DC 26, standby

This whimsical vehicle carries a small number of passengers and crew. It’s capable of short bursts of flight, but the weight of the clockwork mechanisms prevents sustained use. The pilot, crew, and passenger all ride on the back, straddling the hull on built-in saddles.

**Weaknesses** [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56) 10 until [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2)
</row>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** fly 30 feet (clockwork)

**Collision** 4d10 (DC 26)

**Wind-Up** (10-minute wind, 10-minute operation, DC 26, standby) Like all clockwork vehicles, a clockwork bumblebee must be wound up in order to operate, and a creature can decrease the operation time by 10 minutes with a successful [Disable Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) check at the listed DC. A clockwork vehicle can be placed into standby mode by its pilot as a 3-action activity. Its operational time doesn't decrease in standby. You can find more info in the wind-up entry [here](/Traits.aspx?ID=331).

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 99 **Price** 30,000 gp --- While the name slightly overstates its size, nonetheless a magical clockwork castle is a sizable mobile fortress built on ten spiderlike clockwork legs, with three stories of palatial accommodations within. Legends tell of a unique clockwork castle massively larger even than this size, perhaps an artifact in its own right. --- **Space** 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, 35 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 2 crew **Passengers** 10 **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 35), [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (DC 39), or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 37) --- **AC** 36 **Fort** +28 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 250 (BT 125) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 40 feet ([clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=874), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 11d10 (DC 35) **Environmental Protections** This vehicle’s interior temperature is magically maintained. Creatures inside this vehicle are protected from severe cold, severe heat, extreme cold, and extreme heat.
**Luxurious Accommodations** This vehicle contains a bridge, engineering room, private sleeping quarters for up to 13 creatures, and four additional rooms (typically a dining room, kitchen, lavatory, and meeting room).
**Maneuverable** This vehicle is mounted on ten spider-like legs that enable it to turn swiftly, turn in place, and even move backward. Each 90-degree turn made in less than a vehicle length costs 5 extra feet of movement; so, for example, it costs 10 feet of movement for the vehicle to turn around and begin moving backward. This vehicle loses these benefits when broken.
**Skewering Step** ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540)) Two crew members each perform a 3-action activity on their turn to skewer nearby enemies with the clockwork castle’s legs. All creatures under or adjacent to the vehicle at the end of the second character’s turn take 7d8 piercing damage (DC 35 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).
**Weapon Mounts** This vehicle has four rooftop weapon mounts; one mount on each corner of the vehicle. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a weapon mount requires 10 minutes, a successful DC 35 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check, and an appropriate weapon. Three of these weapon mounts can be equipped with ranged weapons, and the fourth can be equipped with a ranged siege weapon of size Large or smaller.
**Wind-Up** 10 minutes of wind-up, 1 hour of operational time, DC 35, standby

fields.text: Vehicle 16 Clockwork Castle Rare Gargantuan Source Guns & Gears (Remastered) pg. 99 Price 30,000 gp While the name slightly overstates its size, nonetheless a magical clockwork castle is a sizable mobile fortress built on ten spiderlike clockwork legs, with three stories of palatial accommodations within. Legends tell of a unique clockwork castle massively larger even than this size, perhaps an artifact in its own right. Space 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, 35 feet high Crew 1 pilot, 2 crew Passengers 10 Piloting Check Driving Lore (DC 35), Arcana (DC 39), or Crafting (DC 37) AC 36 Fort +28 Hardness 20 HP 250 (BT 125) Immunities object immunities Speed 40 feet (clockwork, magical) Collision 11d10 (DC 35) Environmental Protections This vehicle's interior temperature is magically maintained. Creatures inside this vehicle are protected from severe cold, severe heat, extreme cold, and extreme heat. Luxurious Accommodations This vehicle contains a bridge, engineering room, private sleeping quarters for up to 13 creatures, and four additional rooms (typically a dining room, kitchen, lavatory, and meeting room). Maneuverable This vehicle is mounted on ten spider-like legs that enable it to turn swiftly, turn in place, and even move backward. Each 90-degree turn made in less than a vehicle length costs 5 extra feet of movement; so, for example, it costs 10 feet of movement for the vehicle to turn around and begin moving backward. This vehicle loses these benefits when broken. Skewering Step Three Actions (attack) Two crew members each perform a 3-action activity on their turn to skewer nearby enemies with the clockwork castle's legs. All creatures under or adjacent to the vehicle at the end of the second character's turn take 7d8 piercing damage (DC 35 basic Reflex save). Weapon Mounts This vehicle has four rooftop weapon mounts; one mount on each corner of the vehicle. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a weapon mount requires 10 minutes, a successful DC 35 Crafting check, and an appropriate weapon. Three of these weapon mounts can be equipped with ranged weapons, and the fourth can be equipped with a ranged siege weapon of size Large or smaller. Wind-Up 10 minutes of wind-up, 1 hour of operational time, DC 35, standby

While the initial idea is impressive and the cost of creating one is surprisingly low, these junkers, unfortunately, have a strong tendency to malfunction, and they’re always one bad bump away from disaster. --- **Space** 10 feet long, 5 feet wide, 5 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot **Passengers** 1 **Piloting Check** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **AC** 13 **Fort** +7 **Hardness** 5 **HP** 18 (BT 9) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 30 feet (alchemical) **Collision** 2d6 (DC 15) **Fall Apart** When this vehicle takes physical damage the pilot must attempt a DC 11 flat check (or a DC 20 flat check when it takes a critical hit). On a failure, the armored hull fractures and the vehicle loses its Hardness and takes a –4 circumstance penalty to AC.
**Smog** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604)) 10 feet. Whenever this vehicle is being piloted, it continually emits a thin haze of smoke and chemicals. Creatures in the aura (including the pilot and passengers) take a –1 circumstance penalty to visual Perception checks. Volatile
**Flamethrower** (fire) The pilot performs a three‑action activity on their turn to vent alchemical fire out the sides of this vehicle. This requires three flasks of minor [alchemist’s fire](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3287), which the pilot loads into the vent as part of the activity. The pilot must then attempt a DC 5 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). On a success, creatures adjacent to this vehicle take 1d8 fire damage (DC 15 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). On a failure, it backfires, dealing 1d8 fire damage to the pilot and any passengers, with no save.

fields.text: Vehicle 13 Combat Catamaran Gargantuan Source Battlecry! pg. 112 Price 9,000 gp This high-speed sailing ship is designed to track down fleeing vessels. When traveling downwind, the combat catamaran can deploy a pair of huge kite-like spinnakers that dramatically increase its speed. Space 40 feet long, 40 feet wide, 80 feet high Crew 2 pilot, 5 crew Passengers 15 Piloting Check Nature (DC 33) or Sailing Lore (DC 31) AC 29 Fort +23 Hardness 20 HP 230 (BT 115) Immunities object immunities Weaknesses 10 fire until broken Speed swim 30 feet or 50 feet using spinnakers (wind) Collision 9d10 (DC 31) Deploy Spinnakers Three Actions (manipulate) This vehicle has massive kite-like spinnakers. Deploying and retracting these spinnakers takes two crew members to each perform a 3-action activity on their turn. While the spinnakers are deployed, the weapons installed on the weapon mounts can’t fire. Weapon Mounts This vehicle has 2 weapon mounts, with one on each of its hulls. <traits>

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 111

**Price** 270,000 gp

---

An army travels on its stomach, and this wagon train is designed to keep that stomach full. Composed of five heavy wagons connected via a series of flexible corridors, this caravan carries provisions and provides dining services for troops. The lead and middle wagons contain full-service galleys while the second and fourth wagons are stocked to the brim with foodstuffs. The last wagon in the caravan contains a boiler and scullery services for cleaning kitchen utensils and dishes. On the roof of each wagon is an herb garden to ensure a fresh supply for all meals, and mounted beneath all wagons are water and beer storage. Each cook’s caravan carries enough supplies to feed its crew, passengers, 12 Large creatures, and 500 soldiers for a month before needing to be restocked.

---

</column>

<title level="1" right="Vehicle 15">[Djong](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=85)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gargantuan" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 267

**Price** 17,000 gp

</column>

---

Djongs are immense multi-decked outriggers used by the Tian-Sing for transit within the Minata archipelago. Similar in design to the smaller karakoa, djongs have an open hull design that makes them very fast and exceptionally stable, capable of carrying hundreds of rowers on their decks, as well as a large woven triangular sail on a mast. The broad platforms on the djongs made them excellent for ferrying cargo, and their size and stability enabled them to host hundreds of warriors and their gear for transport. During peacetime, djongs are often used to host major celebrations and important weddings, with dignitaries bringing large entourages on their own djongs and then rafting up with other celebrants to form a floating village.

 The size of the djongs is limited by the availability of the large timber required to form each of its twin hulls. Many of the giant trees suitable to build djongs have been harvested, making the surviving djongs even more valuable, with their overall length becoming a metric of status for their owners.

---

**Space** 250 feet long, 100 feet wide, 50 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 400 rowers

**Passengers** 100

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 94 **Price** 450 gp --- A firefly blends magic and technology, using electricity magic and magnetism to hover just above the ground. While a firefly is more box-like than insect-shaped, it gets its name from the constant glow of the light and electricity magic that power it, as well as from the stabilizing magnets that protrude from its sides in roughly the same position as wings would be. --- **Space** 10 feet long, 10 feet wide, 10 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot **Passengers** 3 **Piloting Check** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **AC** 16 **Fort** +12 **Hardness** 5 **HP** 60 (BT 30) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** hover 20 feet (electrical, magical) **Collision** 3d8 (DC 20) **Flash** ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640)) The pilot overcharges the vehicle, causing it to create a brilliant flash of light. All creatures in the bright light from its glow aura must succeed at a DC 19 Fortitude save or be [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) 1 minute. The firefly’s light dims for 10 minutes, reducing its glow to 10 feet of dim light, during which time it can’t use flash. Flash stops working if the firefly is [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60).
**Glow** ([electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), light, [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) Powered by magical lightning, this vehicle sheds bright light within 20 feet, and dim light for a further 20 feet.
**Hover** This vehicle is held aloft by rapidly spinning propellers that enable it to hover 1 foot in the air. It is incapable of flying any higher, and when the pilot stops the magic or the vehicle breaks, it descends 1 foot to the ground.

While a firefly is more box-like than insect-shaped, it gets its name from the constant glow of the light and electricity magic that power it, as well as from the stabilizing magnets that protrude from its sides in roughly the same position as wings would be. All creatures in the bright light from its glow aura must succeed at a DC 19 Fortitude save or be dazzled 1 minute. The floating camouflage blind comprises a wooden platform fastened to a pair of pontoons and is powered by a small clockwork motor. On this platform are four short walls, with a canvas cover providing protection from the elements. Typically, the outside of the blind is painted to blend in with any surrounding foliage. Floating camouflage blinds are often placed near the mouth of strategic waterways so that traffic can be stealthily monitored.

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 113 **Price** 55,000 gp --- This tubular vehicle flies with the aid of a pair of large gas-inflated balloons. With a clockwork-powered aft propeller, the vehicle can move forward if there are no extreme headwinds. Upon landing in the water, the balloons are deflated and stowed within the vehicle, while the aft propeller continues to move it on the surface of the water. By filling a long ballast tank in the vehicle’s keel, it can then submerge and travel underwater. The vehicle can stay submerged for only 1 hour until it must resurface to refresh its oxygen supply. The weapons of this vehicle are in a special compartment that allows them to be fired and reloaded underwater. --- **Space** 60 feet long, 40 feet wide, 40 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 3 crew **Passengers** 30 **Piloting Check** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) (DC 38), [Piloting Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 38), Sailing Lore (DC 36) --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +30 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 280 (BT 140) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) **Weaknesses** fire 10 until [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) --- **Speed** swim 30 ([alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528), [clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=331)) **Collision** 11d10 (DC 36) **Amphibious** This vehicle can land on water and then submerge up to a depth of 200 feet.
**Deploy Balloons** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The pilot engages a lever that activates the clockwork components to launch two massive tethered balloons and fill them with lighter-than-air gas. This grants the flying submersible a fly Speed of 30 but removes its swim Speed. This transformation lasts until the pilot disengages the balloons by performing this action again.
**Weapon Mounts** This vehicle has two weapon mounts. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a mount requires 1 day, a successful DC 36 Crafting check, and an appropriate weapon. The weapon mounts can be equipped with Huge or smaller ranged siege weapons.

**Source** [Tian Xia World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=223) pg. 267 **Price** 6,000 gp --- These squat vessels are built with a protective shell- like covering on their deck rather than the open main deck design of most sailing vessels. The fully covered deck protects the vessel's 80 rowers and complement of 50 soldiers from arrows and incendiary weapons. In addition, this armored deck is covered with iron spikes to discourage enemies from attempting to board. On the bow of the vessel is mounted a dragon head which can emit sulfur smoke to effectively hide its movement in close combat. Below the dragon head is mounted a large anchor with a wooden crest shaped like a face, and these can be used to ram into enemy ships. --- **Space** 110 feet long, 35 feet wide, 40 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 80 rowers **Passengers** 50 **Piloting Check** [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 30), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 32), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 32) --- **AC** 23 **Fort** +18 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 180 (BT 90) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage --- **Speed** swim 30 feet (rowed, wind) **Collision** 8d10 (DC 30) **Smoking Breath** When the geobukseon Stops, it's concealed by the smoke for 1 round or until it next moves. The geobukseon can't use this concealment to Hide or Sneak.
**Turtleback Spikes** The roof of a geobukseon is difficult terrain and hazardous terrain. A creature that moves on the roof takes 1d6 piercing damage for every square of that area it moves into. Falling prone on the geobukseon's roof deals 5d6 piercing damage.

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 76 **Price** 30,000 gp --- **Space** 65 feet long, 65 feet wide, 130 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 200 turners, 3,000 pushers **Passengers** 306 **Piloting Check** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 37), [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 37), or [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 35) --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +28 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 240 (BT 120) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 10 feet (pushed, turned) **Collision** 8d10 (DC 32) **Sluggish** This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.
**Tiered** A helepolis has six levels. The crew operate at the bottom tier, turning a giant capstan. There’s room remaining on that tier for up to six passengers (enough for a full heavy ballista siege crew; see Weaponry). Each of the remaining five levels carries up to 60 passengers. The tiers are specifically meant to be protective and give those within the helepolis greater cover (or standard cover if the helepolis is broken). A massive ladder runs diagonally through the center of the helepolis, from the front of the top tier to the rear of the bottom tier. The ladder is wide enough for two crew or passengers to climb simultaneously.
**Weaponry** The siege tower is loaded to the brim with siege weapons—typically bristling with heavy ballistas on its first and second tiers and ballistas on its third, fourth, and fifth. The Price of these weapons is included in that of the helepolis. When building a helepolis, you can choose to replace any of these with other siege weapons with a lower Price. If you want a more expensive siege weapon, you must [Craft](/Rules.aspx?ID=2634) it separately. Because of the helepolis’s structure, any siege weapon in it must launch its payload straight ahead. For instance, a ballista or springald could function in a helepolis, but not a catapult or trebuchet. Passengers of the helepolis can crew these siege weapons.

<traits>

</column>

---

This imposing warship is known for transforming into an ironclad juggernaut when plates of blackened iron covered in spikes are lowered over its rowing ports. Most hellclad triremes have threatening figureheads shaped like screaming devils.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 120 feet long, 15 feet wide, 25 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 10 crew, 10 rowers

**Passengers** 20
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Sailing Lore (DC 31)](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 33), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 33)

**Fort** +23

</row>

<row gap="medium">

**HP** 200 (BT 100)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

**Weaknesses** 15 fire until broken
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** swim 30 feet (rowed, wind)

**Collision** 9d10 (DC 31)

**Armor of Nessus** Over the course of 1 minute, the ship's crew lowers spiky metal plates across key sections of the hull. The ship gains a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC and immunity to precision damage. Its collision damage becomes piercing damage. Its weakness to fire is reduced to 5, but its swim Speed is reduced to 15 feet and it can no longer be rowed. The crew can retract the plates by taking another minute.

 **Weapon Mounts** This vehicle has 2 weapon mounts, one on each side of the vehicle. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a mount requires 1 day, a successful DC 31 Crafting check, and an appropriate weapon. The weapon mounts can be equipped with Huge or smaller ranged [siege weapons](/SiegeWeapons.aspx).

</column>

---

Karakoa are large twin-hulled outriggers used by the Tian-Sing for transit within the massive Minata archipelago. Fast and sturdy, karakoa are distinct from other Tian vessels in that they're equipped with platforms for transporting warriors and fighting at sea. During peacetime, they're also used as trading ships, able to carry goods and passengers. While capable of crossing oceans, their open hull design may perform poorly during rough seas as breaking whitecaps could swamp the craft.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 225 **Price** 19,500 gp --- A planar skiff is a flat-bottomed ship designed to travel the Great Beyond. A wide variety of skiffs course the planes, with designs incorporating their home planes' fashions and materials. Their magical sails allow them to catch planar currents, and their wards protect travelers as they move across planar boundaries. To allow travel to multiple planes, a _planar skiff_ can have multiple planar keys installed (including items like a _[cipher of the elemental planes](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2652)_). Installing or removing one takes 10 minutes. A planar skiff is typically built with one planar key from its plane of manufacture and a second for a destination plane. --- **Space** 30 feet long, 15 feet wide, 20 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 3 crew **Passengers** 6 **Piloting Check** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) (DC 36), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) (DC 36), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (DC 36), [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (DC 36), or [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) (DC 34) --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +26 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 230 (BT 115) **Immunities** object immunities **Resistances** acid 15, cold 15, electricity 15, fire 15, sonic 15 --- **Speed** fly 50 feet (magical) **Collision** 9d10 (DC 32) **Adaptation Aura** ([aura](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=5)) 10 feet. The vehicle has a warding aura that protects its passengers. Creatures and objects in the aura gain resistance 10 to acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, sonic, vitality, and void damage. They are also protected from [severe cold, severe heat, extreme cold, and extreme heat](/Rules.aspx?ID=642). The aura also provides breathable air for all passengers, though this air can still become filled with smoke and similar substances.
**Journey the Planes** (10 minutes) The pilot locks onto a plane, using one of the vehicle's planar keys as a focus. A canal of planar energy from the destination plane appears ahead of the ship. The pilot spends 10 minutes navigating the passage, then attempts a piloting check (typically DC 34). On a success, the vehicle casts [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=222), transporting itself and all passengers and cargo to the destination plane as it reaches the terminus of the canal. The pilot is considered the target of the spell for the purposes of determining the location at which the vehicle arrives on the plane. The skiff can't _interplanar teleport_ again for 8 hours.
**Planar Evacuation** ([move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114), [reckless](/Traits.aspx?ID=285)) The pilot overcharges one of the vehicle's planar keys, forcing an emergency transport of the ship. The pilot attempts a DC 44 piloting check. On a success, the vehicle casts _interplanar teleport_ as noted in Journey the Planes. (The pilot can't succeed on the check if the vessel is unable to _interplanar teleport_.) This process severely taxes the vehicle, and it can't _interplanar teleport_ again for 1d4 days.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Vehicle 20">[Provarion](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=151)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Gargantuan" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 146

</column>

---

The _Provarion_ is an astounding work of magical engineering known as an ether ship. These vessels were highly valued in ancient Azlant for their capability of traveling between planes. The most famous ether ship was an immense vessel called King Xeros of Old Azlant, but other smaller ether ships like the _Provarion_ existed as well. The exact capabilities of each ether ship varied, but they were similar in many ways to those of the _Provarion_.

The _Provarion_ functions fully well as a [sailing ship](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=79) even without any of its magical abilities. The fact that, as an ether ship, the _Provarion_ is highly resistant to destruction certainly gave it an advantage to those who would ply dangerous waters, but such protection wouldn’t have protected the ship from being swamped, capsized, or dragged to the bottom of the sea by rogue waves, powerful storms, or immense sea monsters. Other ether ships met such fates, but the _Provarion’s_ destiny was to be buried below Absalom in the Sanctum of [Aroden](/Deities.aspx?ID=512).

As with all ether ships, the _Provarion’s_ magical abilities cannot be activated unless three smaller artifacts—a cubic helm, a set of ether sails, and a phase spike—are installed in the ship. (The supernaturally light ether sails are still 10 Bulk, the 15-foot-long phase spike is 8 Bulk, and the missing cubic helm is 2 Bulk.) In the _Provarion’s_ case, two of these artifacts can be found on deck, but the third, a cubic helm, is missing (page 135). These three items are interchangeable between ether ships, so one could, in theory, salvage replacements from other ether ships—if such ships could even be found in the first place. These three artifacts have no function on their own and must be installed in an ether ship like the _Provarion_ to grant the following activations.

**Activate—Into the Great Beyond** 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)); **Requirements** The _Provarion_ is outfitted with ether sails and a cubic helm, and Plot Course has been used to prepare for the journey; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** By concentrating on the cubic helm and spending 10 minutes adjusting and rotating the artifact at the ship’s aftercastle, the _Provarion_ casts [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) to your specifications, transporting it and every creature on board to a planar destination on the plane to which the ether sails are plotted toward. This includes anything Huge or smaller clinging to the ship’s sides, or any creature located in the air amid the ship’s rigging or located above the deck but below its highest mast. If the ship isn’t flying at the time, it appears on the closest body of liquid capable of supporting it within 1d20 × 25 miles of your destination—or if no such body of liquid is available, it becomes beached on the ground. The ship’s ether sails function as the planar key for the destination plane.

**Activate—Plot Course** 10 minutes (concentrate, manipulate, [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=658)); **Requirements** The _Provarion_ is outfitted with ether sails; **Effect** You spend 10 minutes moving among the ship’s rigging and sails, making minute adjustments to their positioning so that they’re in the precise orientation to allow passage to another plane. As you Plot Course, you select which plane the sails are directed toward, choosing from any of the [planes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3014), with the exception of the [Dimension of Time](/Planes.aspx?ID=46). To travel to the Dimension of Time or other planes not listed here, you must also have a planar key for the destination plane, which must be affixed to the _Provarion’s_ mast as part of this activation.

**Activate—Soar Above** <actions string="Three Actions" /> (concentrate, manipulate) **Requirements** The _Provarion_ is outfitted with ether sails and a phase spike, and you are stationed at the Provarion’s wheel; Effect You command the ether sails to fill with magic and lift the _Provarion_ into the air, granting the ship a magical [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 40 feet. This effect ends as soon as you land on something capable of supporting the _Provarion_ (liquid or otherwise). The _Provarion_ continues its forward speed and course if you don’t continue to direct its flight with Soar Above, but each round it does so, its altitude decreases by a distance equal to the distance it traveled on the previous round. If _Provarion_ is commanded via Soar Above to slow to a stop, it can remain afloat indefinitely (barring being dashed about by weather, other vessels, or immense flying creatures).

---

 **Destruction** The _Provarion_ can be destroyed if it is used to sail into the heart of the [Maelstrom](/Planes.aspx?ID=43) and is then used to travel to [Creation’s Forge](/Planes.aspx?ID=27)—doing so reduces the ship to raw soulstuff and scatters any incidental items and creatures on board across the [Great Beyond](/Rules.aspx?ID=2995), with the exception of the ship’s cubic helm, ether sails, and phase spike: these artifacts are destroyed as well alongside the _Provarion_.

fields.text: Vehicle 20 Provarion Unique Gargantuan Artifact Divine Source The Dead God's Hand pg. 146 The Provarion is an astounding work of magical engineering known as an ether ship. These vessels were highly valued in ancient Azlant for their capability of traveling between planes. The most famous ether ship was an immense vessel called King Xeros of Old Azlant, but other smaller ether ships like the Provarion existed as well. The exact capabilities of each ether ship varied, but they were similar in many ways to those of the Provarion . The Provarion functions fully well as a sailing ship even without any of its magical abilities. The fact that, as an ether ship, the Provarion is highly resistant to destruction certainly gave it an advantage to those who would ply dangerous waters, but such protection wouldn’t have protected the ship from being swamped, capsized, or dragged to the bottom of the sea by rogue waves, powerful storms, or immense sea monsters. Other ether ships met such fates, but the Provarion’s destiny was to be buried below Absalom in the Sanctum of Aroden. As with all ether ships, the Provarion’s magical abilities cannot be activated unless three smaller artifacts—a cubic helm, a set of ether sails, and a phase spike—are installed in the ship. (The supernaturally light ether sails are still 10 Bulk, the 15-foot-long phase spike is 8 Bulk, and the missing cubic helm is 2 Bulk.) In the Provarion’s case, two of these artifacts can be found on deck, but the third, a cubic helm, is missing (page 135). These three items are interchangeable between ether ships, so one could, in theory, salvage replacements from other ether ships—if such ships could even be found in the first place. These three artifacts have no function on their own and must be installed in an ether ship like the Provarion to grant the following activations. Activate—Into the Great Beyond 10 minutes (concentrate, manipulate); Requirements The Provarion is outfitted with ether sails and a cubic helm, and Plot Course has been used to prepare for the journey; Frequency once per day; Effect By concentrating on the cubic helm and spending 10 minutes adjusting and rotating the artifact at the ship’s aftercastle, the Provarion casts interplanar teleport to your specifications, transporting it and every creature on board to a planar destination on the plane to which the ether sails are plotted toward. This includes anything Huge or smaller clinging to the ship’s sides, or any creature located in the air amid the ship’s rigging or located above the deck but below its highest mast. If the ship isn’t flying at the time, it appears on the closest body of liquid capable of supporting it within 1d20 × 25 miles of your destination—or if no such body of liquid is available, it becomes beached on the ground. The ship’s ether sails function as the planar key for the destination plane. Activate—Plot Course 10 minutes (concentrate, manipulate, move); Requirements The Provarion is outfitted with ether sails; Effect You spend 10 minutes moving among the ship’s rigging and sails, making minute adjustments to their positioning so that they’re in the precise orientation to allow passage to another plane. As you Plot Course, you select which plane the sails are directed toward, choosing from any of the planes, with the exception of the Dimension of Time. To travel to the Dimension of Time or other planes not listed here, you must also have a planar key for the destination plane, which must be affixed to the Provarion’s mast as part of this activation. Activate—Soar Above Three Actions (concentrate, manipulate) Requirements The Provarion is outfitted with ether sails and a phase spike, and you are stationed at the Provarion’s wheel; Effect You command the ether sails to fill with magic and lift the Provarion into the air, granting the ship a magical fly Speed of 40 feet. This effect ends as soon as you land on something capable of supporting the Provarion (liquid or otherwise). The Provarion continues its forward speed and course if you don’t continue to direct its flight with Soar Above, but each round it does so, its altitude decreases by a distance equal to the distance it traveled on the previous round. If Provarion is commanded via Soar Above to slow to a stop, it can remain afloat indefinitely (barring being dashed about by weather, other vessels, or immense flying creatures). Destruction The Provarion can be destroyed if it is used to sail into the heart of the Maelstrom and is then used to travel to Creation’s Forge—doing so reduces the ship to raw soulstuff and scatters any incidental items and creatures on board across the Great Beyond, with the exception of the ship’s cubic helm, ether sails, and phase spike: these artifacts are destroyed as well alongside the Provarion . Space 75 feet long, 20 feet wide, 25 feet high Crew 1 pilot, 8 crew Passengers 10 Piloting Check Sailing Lore (DC 26), Diplomacy (DC 28), or Intimidation (DC 28) AC 23 Fort +18 Hardness 15 HP 150 (BT 75) Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage Speed swim 40 feet (wind) Collision 6d10 (DC 26) Sluggish This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.

Both of those creatures take 6d6 fire damage from the sand racer's burning exhaust (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).
**Success** As critical success, but choose only one creature.
**Failure** As success, but the creature gains a +4 circumstance bonus to its Reflex save, and the sand racer moves its Speed in a straight line.
**Critical Failure** You fail to blast any creatures with the burning exhaust. The sand racer moves its Speed in a straight line and becomes uncontrolled.
**Exploratory Kit** Sand racers were built to aid in long-distance exploration of Akiton's sandy wastelands, and have storage capacity for 14 days of [rations](/Equipment.aspx?ID=40) for a Medium creature and 14 days of fuel. They also have a small storage compartment in the front designed to store a [repair kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=43) and replacement parts for the more delicate pieces of machinery.
**Speed Boost** **Frequency** once per 10 minutes; **Effect** The pilot triggers an injection of thasteron directly into the sand racer's engine to briefly increase its speed. For 1 round the sand racer's Speed becomes 180 feet, all piloting checks with the sand racer gain the [reckless](/Traits.aspx?ID=285) trait, and the pilot gains a +2 circumstance to any [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) or piloting checks made to navigate specific challenges. A speed boost is terribly inefficient, and consumes a day's worth of fuel.

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 105 **Price** 3,500 gp --- Enormous masses of steel kept afloat by magic, sea forts were originally developed by the Corentyn armada to enforce blockades. While not particularly fast or maneuverable, their high resistance to damage and ability to expand their reach with additional walls makes them difficult to ignore. Armadas often keep them anchored to shield a narrow channel or vulnerable land target or use them to shield smaller and nimbler craft as they prepare an attack. --- **Space** 150 feet long, 25 feet wide, 30 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 8 crew **Passengers** 10 **Piloting Check** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (DC 29) or [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 27) --- **AC** 26 **Fort** +10 **Hardness** 15 **HP** 180 (BT 90) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** swim 15 feet ([magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 7d10 (DC 27) **Extend Blockade** The pilot deploys steel walls that extend from the hull of the ship by 50 feet in each direction, increasing its length to 250 feet. The _sea fort_ can Extend Blockade only while its swim Speed is 0, and Extend Blockade can't be active at the same time as Raise Ramparts.
**Hunker Down** The pilot drops the _sea fort's_ anchor, reducing its swim Speed to 0 and securing it to its current position in the sea. While anchored, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to its AC and Fortitude saving throws. The pilot can use this activity again to raise the anchor.
**Raise Ramparts** The pilot deploys magnetized steel walls that extend from the _sea fort's_ sides, increasing its height to 60 feet. The ramparts have an AC of 20, Hardness 10, and 80 HP (BT 40). Thanks to the magnetic runes, metal projectiles fired at the _sea fort_ strike the ramparts first and can't damage the ship itself until they're broken. The _sea fort_ can Raise Ramparts only while its swim Speed is 0, and Raise Ramparts can't be active at the same time as Extended Blockade. If the ramparts are destroyed, Raise Ramparts can't be used until they're repaired.

**Source** [Cheliax, Infernal Inheritence](/Sources.aspx?ID=372) pg. 105 **Price** 900 gp --- A _shadow chaser_ can move above or below the water's surface, gathering information about ships and aquatic creatures using stealthy magic. _Shadow chasers_ are designed for observation rather than direct combat, often luring pursuers into conflict with more heavily armed surface vessels. --- **Space** 60 feet long, 10 feet wide, 10 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 4 crew **Passengers** 4 **Piloting Check** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (DC 24), [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 22), or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) (DC 24) --- **AC** 18 **Fort** +13 **Hardness** 10 **HP** 80 (BT 40) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** swim 40 feet ([magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 4d10 (DC 22) Air Bubble **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** The pilot activates runes that generate an air bubble around the ship for 10 minutes. The thickened air allows creatures on board to breathe while the _shadow chaser_ is Submerged and deflects projectiles, granting the vehicle a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against physical ranged attacks.
**Submerge** The shadow chaser sinks 20 feet below the water's surface, becoming [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) to all creatures and objects on the surface. This activity can be used again to return to the surface, and if the vehicle is below another creature or object, the contact is treated as a collision.

**Tiered** A siege tower has five levels. The bottom level houses the crew, and each higher level carries up to 10 passengers. The tiers are specifically meant to be protective and give those within the siege tower [greater cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=2372) (or standard cover if the siege tower is broken). Each tier is connected to the one above it by a 7-foot ladder. The siege tower has a corvus at its highest tier: a vertical bridge that can be lowered to allow creatures to cross gaps. Lowering the corvus takes a total of 3 [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) actions. Moving the siege tower while the corvus is lowered is highly dangerous, especially for anyone on the corvus. When it’s open, creatures in the top tier don’t have cover from the side with the corvus, and creatures on the lowered corvus don’t have cover except from below.

Space 20 feet long, 20 feet wide, 40 feet high Crew 1 pilot, 9 pushers Passengers 40 Piloting Check Diplomacy (DC 21), Intimidation (DC 21), or Warfare Lore (DC 19) AC 16 Fort +11 Hardness 10 HP 40 (BT 20) Immunities object immunities Speed 10 feet (pushed by the pushers in the crew) Collision 3d10 (DC 18) Sluggish This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes. Tiered A siege tower has five levels. The bottom level houses the crew, and each higher level carries up to 10 passengers. The tiers are specifically meant to be protective and give those within the siege tower greater cover (or standard cover if the siege tower is broken). Each tier is connected to the one above it by a 7-foot ladder. The siege tower has a corvus at its highest tier: a vertical bridge that can be lowered to allow creatures to cross gaps. Lowering the corvus takes a total of 3 Interact actions. Moving the siege tower while the corvus is lowered is highly dangerous, especially for anyone on the corvus. When it's open, creatures in the top tier don't have cover from the side with the corvus, and creatures on the lowered corvus don't have cover except from below.

<title level="1" right="Vehicle 11">[Skimmer](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=114)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Huge" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 115

**Price** 4,000 gp

</column>

---

This sleek vessel generally appears as a fast-moving catamaran. Using a pair of clockwork mechanisms, the main hulls can be lifted out of the water, with only the narrow blade of their keels remaining slightly below the surface, turning the skimmer into an even faster hydrofoil, doubling its normal speed.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 20 feet long, 15 feet wide, 35 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 3 crew

**Passengers** 2
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) (DC 30) or [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 28)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 24

**Fort** +19

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 15

**HP** 150 (BT 75)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

**Weaknesses** fire 5 until [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60)
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** swim 30 feet or 60 feet using hydrofoil (wind)

**Collision** 7d10 (DC 28)

**Deploy Hydrofoil** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) The skimmer’s hydrofoils are deployed by pulling a lever, doubling the vehicle’s normal Speed. However, this makes the vehicle less maneuverable, and it must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes while the hydrofoils are deployed. The pilot can take this action again to retract the hydrofoils and return the skimmer to its normal Speed and maneuverability.

</column>

</traits>

</column>

---

This open-air vehicle is constructed similar to a sleigh, with four wheels in the place of runners and a set of sweeping wings extending from its sides. The wooden body of the vehicle is armored to protect the occupants, who can fire handheld weapons over the gunwales to gain cover from ranged attacks.

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 2 crew

**Passengers** 4

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">

**Fort** +25

</row>

<row gap="medium">

**HP** 190 (BT 95)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** the fly Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 6 Large creatures, 2 Huge creatures, or 1 Gargantuan creature)

**Collision** 10d10 (DC 32)

**Alchemical Launcher** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) Two crew members each perform a 3-action activity on their turn to launch a massive alchemical concoction from the chariot. The concoction explodes on impact, dealing 10d6 fire damage to each creature in a 15-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) up to 50 feet away (DC 30 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

<title level="1" right="Vehicle 7">[Smuggler's Speronara](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=148)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Huge" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 95

**Price** 1,080 gp

</column>

---

This merchant craft has no deck and only one mast. It has a relatively shallow hull for storing cargo, but also several hidden compartments for smuggling illicit goods.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 45 feet long, 20 feet wide, 15 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 2 crew, 4 rowers

**Passengers** 5
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Sailing Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 23), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 25), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 25)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 21

**Fort** +14

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 10

**HP** 110 (BT 55)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

**Weaknesses** fire 10 until broken
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** swim 30 feet (rowed, wind)

**Collision** 4d10 (DC 23)

**Maneuverable** With a full complement of skilled rowers, a rowed speronara can turn swiftly, turn in place, and even row backward. Each 90-degree turn made in less than a vehicle length costs 5 extra feet of movement. It can row backward no faster than half its speed, and it can't turn while rowing backward.

 **Smuggling** Compartments The speronara can hold up to 20 Bulk of items in secret compartments that require a successful DC 23 Perception check to find.

</column>

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Vehicle 7">[Snail Coach](/Vehicles.aspx?ID=132)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Huge" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 96

**Price** 1,000 gp

</column>

---

Shaped like its animal namesake, a snail coach is a trolley powered by a combination of magic and alchemical adhesives, with a hard outer shell to protect itself from attacks. The adhesive trail both allows it to climb and leaves a hindrance for pursuing foes.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 30 feet long, 10 feet wide, 15 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 1 crew

**Passengers** 6
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 23) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 25)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 21

**Fort** +15

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 10

**HP** 100 (BT 50)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** 15 feet, climb 15 feet (alchemical, magical)

**Collision** 7d6 (DC 21)

**Adhesive Secretions** This vehicle secretes an alchemical adhesive that allows it to stick to and climb up solid surfaces. Spaces the snail coach moves through become [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) for 1 round. Any creature that ends their turn on the adhesive must succeed at a DC 23 Reflex save or take a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round. On a critical failure, the creature is also [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC 23).

</column>

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 96 **Price** 2,900 gp --- A speedster is a light streamlined hybrid clockwork and steam-powered alchemical chassis roughly the shape of a [horse](/Companions.aspx?ID=76) or other creature built for speed. Speedsters are built to maintain a rapid pace that can become even faster for brief periods of time by releasing stored up steam pressure for an extra burst of speed. --- **Space** 10 feet long, 5 feet wide, 5 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot **Passengers** 1 **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 27) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 29) --- **AC** 23 **Fort** +19 **Hardness** 15 **HP** 130 (BT 65) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 50 feet (alchemical, clockwork) **Collision** 7d10 (DC 27) **Speed Boost** The pilot releases built up pressure in the speedster’s alchemical steam engine in order to temporarily increase its speed. For 1d4 rounds, the speedster’s Speed becomes 80 feet and all move actions the pilot takes gain the [reckless](/Traits.aspx?ID=685) trait. When the pilot takes an action that already would have the reckless trait, the pilot uses the degree of success one worse than the one they rolled on the piloting check. The speedster can’t use Speed Boost again for 1 hour, as the pressure requires time to rebuild.
**Streamlined** This lightweight vehicle has no additional storage space for cargo.
**Wind-Up** 10 minutes of wind-up, 2 hours of operational time, DC 28, standby

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 210,000 gp

</column>

---

A massive red-and-black warship, the _Dark Prince_ sports an imposing figurehead of Asmodeus and terrifying faces carved along its gunwales. It patrols the area around the Arch of Aroden, keeping the waters free of pirates and enemies.

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Space** 280 feet long, 60 feet wide, 30 feet high

<row gap="medium">
**Crew** 1 pilot, 50 crew

**Passengers** 50
</row>

**Piloting Check** [Sailing Lore (DC 40)](/Skills.aspx?ID=41), [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) (DC 42), or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (DC 42)

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

<row gap="medium">
**AC** 42

**Fort** +35

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Hardness** 18

**HP** 320 (BT 160)

**Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161)

**Resistances** 20 fire until broken

</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Speed** swim 20 feet (wind)

**Collision** 14d10 (DC 40)

**Dreadful Aura** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) The flagship of the Chelaxian navy exudes a malevolent air. At the beginning of their turns or when they enter the aura, enemy creatures on board the ship and enemy creatures within a 300-foot-emanation who can see the ship must succeed at a DC 39 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (or frightened 2 on a critical failure). Regardless of the result, the creature is temporarily immune to this aura for 1 minute. However, an enemy creature on board can't reduce its frightened condition below 1 until it is no longer on board.

 **Weapon Mounts** This vehicle has 6 weapon mounts, three on each side of the vehicle. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a mount requires 1 day, a successful DC 40 Crafting check, and an appropriate weapon. The weapon mounts can be equipped with Huge or smaller ranged [siege weapons](/SiegeWeapons.aspx).

</column>

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 98 **Price** 19,000 gp --- Among the most dangerous vehicles created in Ustalav with a mix of magic and the new Stasian technology, a titanic stomper is shaped like a long sinuous lizard or behir with carefully placed Stasian coils and eight big stomping legs. Titanic stompers were meant to devastate the armies of the undead. Only two exist, making them almost unique, and the means to create more have been stymied, as some of the crucial inventors were killed in the process of attempting to design a follow-up technology, a smaller but more powerful suit of mechanized armor called the Grobelarch that ultimately went berserk and killed its creators. --- **Space** 60 feet long, 30 feet wide, 60 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 3 crew **Passengers** 6 **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 34) or [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 36) --- **AC** 34 **Fort** +26 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 230 (BT 115) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 40 feet, (electrical, magical) **Collision** 9d12 (DC 32) **Bolt Blast** Two crew members each perform a three-action activity on their turn to fire a line of lightning at the end of the second character’s turn. This line of lightning erupts from the front of the titanic stomper at an angle of the crew members’ choice and deals 5d12 electricity damage to each creature in a 120-foot line (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). The Bolt Blast stops working if the titanic stomper is broken.
**Electrical Absorption** **Trigger** The titanic stomper is targeted by, or in the area of, an effect that deals electricity damage; **Effect** The pilot uses their reaction to activate the Stasian coils, which funnels the electricity into the titanic stomper’s electrical engine. The next time Bolt Blast is used within the next minute, the damage it deals increases to 7d12.
**Quaking Step** The ground shakes with every step a titanic stomper takes. Whenever this vehicle moves, creatures on the ground within 20 feet of its movement path must attempt a DC 32 Reflex save. On a failure, they are [flat‑footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 round, and on a critical failure, they’re knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=318) pg. 99 **Price** 50,000 gp --- Crafted by the wizard Vonthos as part of his bid to attempt the Test of the _Starstone_ in Absalom, this strange vehicle is considered to be a magical and technological marvel. Vonthos’s Golden Bridge is a flying sphere made out of a throne surrounded by several clockwork rings covered in gold and gems infused with powerful adaptive abjurations that grant it unique abilities. --- **Space** 9 feet long, 9 feet wide, 9 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot **Piloting Check** [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 36) or [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (DC 38) --- **AC** 39 **Fort** +29 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 310 (BT 155) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** fly 40 feet ([clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=874), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) **Collision** 11d10 (DC 36) **Captivating Wealth** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542), [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [magic](/Skills.aspx?ID=27), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) 40 feet. The gold, gems, and other embellishments that adorn this flying sphere emit a sparkling resplendence capable of enthralling creatures. Each creature that begins its turn within the aura must attempt a DC 36 Will save; on a failure, the creature is fascinated and stupefied 2 for as long as it remains within the aura. A creature that succeeds is temporarily immune for 1 hour. Each time Prismatic Defense is activated, the area of Captivating Wealth is reduced by 10 feet for 1 hour, to a minimum of 0 feet.
**Protective Barrier** While the swirling rings of the vehicle don’t fully cover the pilot, they offer incredible protection, magically maintaining the temperature within and ablating physical attacks. The pilot is protected from severe cold, severe heat, extreme cold, and extreme heat. The pilot also gains resistance 10 to all physical damage (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2915)).
**Prismatic Defense** ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=644)) The pilot harnesses power from the magical gemstones hidden among this vehicle’s extravagant embellishments to grant the vehicle additional defenses. This vehicle gains resistance 20 to one of the following energy damage types: [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697). This immunity lasts until Prismatic Defense is next activated.
**Wind-Up** 10 minutes of wind-up, 1 hour of operational time, DC 37, standby

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 112 **Price** 63,000 gp --- This massive steam-powered vehicle resembles a giant insect with six articulated legs topped with a bulbous turret capable of swiveling 360 degrees to bring its forward-mounted weapons to bear on enemies in any direction. It has weapon ports on either side of its head that give the appearance of eyes. With its long, mechanized legs, it can easily climb over obstacles and cross wide chasms. --- **Space** 20 feet long, 20 feet wide, 40 feet high **Crew** 1 pilot, 5 crew **Passengers** 10 **Piloting Check** [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (DC 40) or [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) (DC 38) --- **AC** 40 **Fort** +32 **Hardness** 20 **HP** 280 (BT 140) **Immunities** [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161) --- **Speed** 30 feet ([alchemical](/Traits.aspx?ID=528), [clockwork](/Traits.aspx?ID=331)), [ignores difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) **Collision** 12d10 (DC 38) **Long Stride** A war strider can bridge a gap as wide as 30 feet during a move action as long as it has sufficient movement remaining.
**Weapon Mount** This vehicle has two forward-mounted weapon mounts. At purchase, these weapon mounts are initially empty. Installing or uninstalling a weapon into a mount requires 1 day, a successful DC 37 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check, and an appropriate weapon. The weapon mounts can be equipped with Huge or smaller ranged siege weapons.

Space 85 feet long, 25 feet wide, 20 feet high Crew 1 pilot, 10 crew Passengers 30 Piloting Check Sailing Lore (DC 23), Diplomacy (DC 25), or Intimidation (DC 25) AC 22 Fort +17 Hardness 15 HP 150 (BT 75) Immunities object immunities Weaknesses fire 15 until broken Speed swim 30 feet (wind) Collision 6d10 (DC 26) Unfurl Yellow Sails Single Action (emotion, fear, manipulate, mental, visual) With the pull of a rope, the pilot or one of the crew unfurls the yellow sails that Okeno freebooters are so infamous for. Each enemy creature within a 100-foot emanation who can see the sails must succeed at a DC 26 Will save or become frightened 1 (or frightened 2 on a critical failure). Regardless of the save's results, the creature is temporarily immune to Unfurl Yellow Sails for 24 hours.
